Step 4
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 3
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 5
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 4
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 3
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 2
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 4
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. discover_workflow

inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

discover_workflow

inspect_workflow_items

edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. focus_page_element

Step 3
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 2
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

discover_workflow

inspect_workflow_items

edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 3
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Node properties may be omitted when empty. Edge endpoints are source and target, not sourceId and targetId. Atomically applies up to 20 commands. Both createNode node.label and updateNode patch.label accept a string or copied Snapshot label object. On conflict or when recovery directs you, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit. Pass the result's operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence. After it succeeds, briefly tell the user what the operation accomplished and its outcome or implication, not only the changed-object details.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.
